question: During a D&C procedure, immediately after sounding the uterus to a depth of 8 cm, the correct next step is:

answers.text: Gently dilate the cervix with Hegar dilators, beginning with the smallest size and increasing sequentially

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. After sounding the uterus (to determine the direction and depth of the cavity), the cervix is dilated using Hegar dilators starting from the smallest size and progressing sequentially. Forcing a larger dilator without sequential dilation risks cervical laceration or uterine perforation.

answers.text: Insert the largest curettage forceps directly to maximise tissue yield

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Inserting a curette before cervical dilatation risks cervical trauma and uterine perforation. Sequential dilatation is required first.

answers.text: Apply tenacula forceps to the anterior cervical lip to steady the uterus

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The vulsellum or single-toothed tenaculum is applied to the anterior cervical lip before sounding (to straighten the cervico-uterine axis), not after it. Sounding has already been completed in this question.

answers.text: Irrigate the uterine cavity with antiseptic solution before curettage

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Intrauterine irrigation is not a step in the standard D&C technique and may force infection upwards or affect histological yield.

overallFeedback.feedback: D&C sequence: bimanual exam → anaesthesia → tenaculum → sound uterus → SEQUENTIAL dilatation with Hegar dilators → curettage. Never skip sequential dilation.
Correct. After sounding → sequential cervical dilatation with Hegar dilators (smallest to largest) → then curettage.
